instrument: INSTRUMENT NOTE. The first version of `scripts/mutation-probe.mjs` ran `check --json` WITHOUT `--strict`, and the entire evidence layer is unreachable in that mode (`computeVerdict` only calls `judgeGated`, and therefore `evidenceReport`/`evidenceBreakdown`, under `if (opts.strict)`). This was measured here independently before the coordinator's correction arrived: the shipped reference mission with one pointer repointed at a nonexistent file (`file:code/src/core/domain/NOPE.ts#guardFields`) returned exit 0 from `check --json` with a payload byte-identical to the intact mission, and exit 1 from `check --strict --json` with the violation. A 0/24 result from the uncorrected probe was therefore true by construction, not by innocence. Every measurement below was re-run end to end with the CORRECTED `scripts/mutation-probe.mjs` (`gateArgs = ["dist/cli.js", "check", "--strict", "--json", …]`); the pre-correction ledgers were discarded. Each probe mission was also verified by hand on a pristine tree first: `node dist/cli.js check --strict --json --path <mission>` was run and its baseline verdict and violation list read before any mutant was applied. SELF-GATE, with the corrected probe: baseline exit 0, 4479 bytes, **0/24 observable** — and that result is real, not an artefact. runward's own mission cites only the robust forms (`file:PATH#SYMBOL`, bare `test:PATH`), so none of the `:LINE`, `::NAME`, quoted-symbol or multi-pointer branches this function carries is reachable from it, exactly as ADR-0046 already states. The self-gate cannot clear a single one of these 24.

verdicts.evidence: FALSE GREEN, verified by exit code. Applied on m4 (single defect: `file:code/deleted-a.ts<U+2028>; file:code/b.ts`): `check --strict --json` went from **exit 1 to exit 0**, conformance 1 -> 0, and the violation `Floor · tools-scope-atomicity · typed pointer does not resolve: file:code/deleted-a.ts — update it or remove the row` disappeared entirely. Re-observed on m2, where the same mutant removed TWO refusals (conformance 10 -> 8): `file:code/deleted-a.ts` (U+2028 separator) and `file:code/deleted-a2.ts` (CR separator). Mechanism as observed, not as read: when a chunk ends in a line terminator, POINTER_PREFIX's `(\S.*)$` cannot reach `$` (`.` excludes line terminators), the chunk yields no match and the pointer is dropped silently — the row still reads as typed and the cited file is never opened. This is the RWD-2026-0006 family: a pointer that looks precise and verifies nothing. Reachable because `readManifest` only trims the ENDS of a cell, so a terminator sitting before a `;` survives into the chunk. The missing test: a cell whose first pointer is followed by CR or U+2028 and then `; <second pointer>` must still refuse the first pointer's missing file.

verdicts.argument: The comparison is only ever evaluated on the third leg of `sep !== -1 && (firstWs === -1 || sep < firstWs)`: reaching it requires `sep !== -1` AND `firstWs !== -1`, since `firstWs === -1` short-circuits the disjunction to true before the comparison runs. On that path `sep = rest.indexOf("::")`, so `rest[sep]` is the character `:`; and `firstWs = rest.search(/\s/)`, so `rest[firstWs]` is a whitespace character. `:` is not a whitespace character, therefore `sep === firstWs` is unreachable for every possible input string, and `<` and `<=` return the same boolean wherever the expression is evaluated. No mission can distinguish them because no Evidence cell can make a colon be whitespace.

verdicts.argument: The mutated operand is the left half of `symbol !== undefined && /\s/.test(symbol)`. When `symbol` is a string, `symbol !== undefined` is already `true`, so replacing it by `true` changes nothing. When `symbol` is `undefined`, the original short-circuits the conjunction to `false`; the mutant instead evaluates `/\s/.test(undefined)`, and `RegExp.prototype.test` coerces its argument with ToString, giving the seven-letter string `"undefined"`, which contains no whitespace — so the test is `false` and the conjunction is `false` too. Both forms therefore select the same branch of the ternary on every input. `symbol` is `string | undefined` by construction (it is assigned only from `quoted[3] || undefined` and from `token.slice(hash + 1) || undefined`), so `undefined` is the only non-string value it can hold and no other coercion is reachable; the regex has no `g` flag, so `test` has no side effect either. No mission can distinguish them.
